rv.q: Christian’s composition for twelve voices was back, and the long delay had seemingly refined it to a diamond intensity.
Oratorio for Living Things remains one of the most beautiful, profound, and altogether astonishing musical-theater works of recent years.
An indescribably strange and beautiful musical meditation on time.
Together, the music and movement of Oratorio for Living Things create something vast, intimate, and spectacular.
I found the Signature iteration profoundly moving in both its intimacy and artistry.
On the other hand, if just being engulfed by gorgeous music, delightful singing is wanted, Oratorio for Living Things is the place to be.
Signature Theatre's Resident Heather Christian has brought a complex yet humble and angelic space for us to simultaneously feel and lose ourselves in time.

cn.t: Critics largely rave over Heather Christian's immersive musical meditation on time, praising its sweeping blend of jazz, soul, and gospel across 12 voices. One dissenting view finds it uneven, but most call it a must-see masterpiece.

vr.q: I do think it's a must see, especially if you're into choral or gospel music.
